claims.text: Melilot, or Sweet Clover, is a grassland plant. The name derives from Greek μελίλωτος "honey lotus".
claims.cite: Jim Allan (ed.), An Introduction to Elvish, "Giving of Names"; see also J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "III. The Lay of Leithian", p. 159

claims.text: Melilot was the daughter of Marmadas Brandybuck. She was present at Bilbo's Birthday Party in , when she was just sixteen years old. The only part she played in the great events of that time was to dance the springle-ring at the party with Everard Took.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "Brandybuck of Buckland"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring, "A Long-expected Party"

claims.text: In an early version of the legendarium, Melilot was a tentative name for the character later known as Lúthien Tinúviel.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "III. The Lay of Leithian", p. 159
